solved.topic: Hess's law - enthalpy of formation from combustion data
solved.q: Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of methane, CH4(g), given: C(s) + O2(g) -> CO2(g), dH1 = -394 kJ/mol; H2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) -> H2O(l), dH2 = -286 kJ/mol; CH4(g) + 2O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2H2O(l), dH3 = -890 kJ/mol.
steps: Given: dH1 = -394 kJ/mol, dH2 = -286 kJ/mol, dH3 = -890 kJ/mol.
Target reaction: C(s) + 2H2(g) -> CH4(g), so dHf(CH4) = dH1 + 2(dH2) - dH3 (by Hess's law, adding reactions 1 and twice reaction 2, then subtracting reaction 3 to cancel CO2 and H2O).

solved.q: For a reaction, dH = +50 kJ/mol and dS = +100 J/K/mol at T = 400 K. Calculate dG and state whether the reaction is spontaneous.
steps: Given: dH = 50 kJ/mol = 50000 J/mol, dS = 100 J/K/mol, T = 400 K.
Answer: dG = +10 kJ/mol; since dG > 0, the reaction is non-spontaneous at 400 K.

solved.topic: Temperature at which a reaction becomes spontaneous
solved.q: A reaction has dH = +60 kJ/mol and dS = +150 J/K/mol. Find the minimum temperature above which the reaction becomes spontaneous.
steps: Given: dH = 60 kJ/mol = 60000 J/mol, dS = 150 J/K/mol.
At the point the reaction just becomes spontaneous, dG = 0, so dH = T dS.
Answer: the reaction becomes spontaneous for T > 400 K.

solved.topic: Entropy change during a phase transition
solved.q: A solid melts at 273 K absorbing 5460 J/mol of heat. Calculate the entropy change of fusion, dSfus.
steps: Given: dHfus = 5460 J/mol, T = 273 K (melting is a reversible, constant-T, constant-P process).

solved.topic: First law of thermodynamics (dU = q + w)
solved.q: A system absorbs 500 J of heat from the surroundings while the surroundings do 200 J of work on the system. Calculate the change in internal energy, dU.
steps: Given: q = +500 J (heat absorbed by system, positive), w = +200 J (work done on the system, positive by sign convention).

solved.topic: Gibbs free energy from equilibrium constant (dG = -2.303RT log K)
solved.q: Calculate the standard Gibbs free energy change, dG, for a reaction at 300 K whose equilibrium constant K = 100. (R = 8.314 J/mol K)
steps: Given: K = 100, so log10(K) = 2; T = 300 K; R = 8.314 J/mol K.
Formula: dG = -2.303 R T log K.
Answer: dG = -11490 J/mol = -11.49 kJ/mol (negative, confirming K > 1 means the reaction is spontaneous).

solved.topic: Enthalpy of reaction from bond enthalpies
solved.q: Using bond enthalpy data, calculate dH for the reaction H2(g) + Cl2(g) -> 2HCl(g). Given bond enthalpies: H-H = 432 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl = 242 kJ/mol, H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol.
steps: Given: bonds broken: 1 mol H-H (432 kJ) + 1 mol Cl-Cl (242 kJ); bonds formed: 2 mol H-Cl (2 x 431 kJ).
Formula: dH = (sum of bond enthalpies of reactants broken) - (sum of bond enthalpies of products formed).

solved.topic: Entropy change from dH and dG
solved.q: For a reaction at 400 K, dH = -184 kJ/mol and dG = -196 kJ/mol. Calculate the entropy change, dS, of the reaction.
steps: Given: dH = -184 kJ/mol = -184000 J/mol, dG = -196 kJ/mol = -196000 J/mol, T = 400 K.
Formula: dG = dH - T dS, rearranged as dS = (dH - dG) / T.
